title: Leaving Hunter; a letter from Spec Redd
summary: Wanting to play drums, Gus left Hunter and accepted Ernest 'Spec' Redd's invitation to Ottumwa, Iowa; Redd was a fine Earl Hines and Tatum imitator.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Well, listen, all right, so after you -- you stayed about a year and a half or not quite that with Lloyd Hunter. And then you were getting a bit fed up because they weren't taking their music seriously enough.
I wanted to really stick with my drums, and I was afraid they wanted me to go back and play bass again, see.
And then I got this letter from Spec Redd.
He was the cousin to Red Perkins.
He used to play in Red Perkins' band. He left Red Perkins to go to Omaha to take a job there.
Oh. Well, what was Red Perkins' instrument? Did he just front a band?
He fronted the band and he played the saxophone, too. But he fronted the band.
Yeah, two territory bands. And, well, now, Ernest Spec Redd -- now, he was his cousin.
And he left, and he's a pianist. Was he a good pianist?
A very good pianist. He can imitate Earl Hines.
And he played a lot of Art Tatum's style, too.
Isn't a shame, in those days a lot of very good musicians that never got to record, who if they had recorded, maybe they'd have been known in the East or --
I don't know why, but Spec, he went
to Ottumwa, Iowa and just stayed there until I left.
And when I left, I came back to Kansas City, --
So when he left Ottumwa, he went to Des Moines.
And he stayed there until last year. That's when he died.
Did he have a good band?
Oh, he always kept a nice group.
But then he got rid of the band, and then he was just doing duet and --
Yeah, and singles and stuff like that.
But he was a very good piano player.
So was he like Earl? Was he like a piano player with a band, that featured the piano.
Well, he must have been pleased to have a good drummer.
In Omaha. He heard me with Lloyd Hunter's band.
Yeah. And he sent for you.
Yes. He was playing with Red Perkins.
Then [one of 'em] he had his own band.
Then he left and went to Ottumwa, Iowa.
So you were in one of his first bands, really.
Because he had just left Red Perkins.
